text:
maya: Heads-up — after the quota migration last night we're seeing sustained 429s for tenant acme-inc on dedicated pool delta. Started ~09:22 UTC and hasn't fallen with autoscale.
jordan: thanks, can you paste the initial error payload and a small timeframe of request patterns? are they short bursts or steady QPS?
sre-bot: ALERT: tenant=acme-inc pool=delta throttle_ratio=0.82 recent_429=120 window=5m
maya: looks bursty, lots of short chat completions (seq len ~40) hitting per-tenant rate window. sample error:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{"error":"rate_exceeded","quota_key":"tenant:acme-inc:dedicated:delta:rate:units"}
```
anita: did the migration change units (minutes vs hours) or accidentally double-applied backfill tokens?
maya: suspect backfill. ops applied a migration script that stamped a backfilled_quota value for historical usage; I see entries in quota_events with large negative timestamps.
ken: quick repro: curl the endpoint with header x-tenant=acme-inc and high concurrency (~50) for 30s. I can run from my laptop but need a safe repro window.
jordan: please don't blast prod. ken, run against a canary replica or run our local harness using `--dedicated-pool=delta --tenant=acme-inc --rate=burst`.
ken: ack. I'll use the harness. sharing the command:
```
./tools/loadgen --pool delta --tenant acme-inc --concurrency 40 --duration 30s --seq-len 40
```
maya: logs show quota key history:
```
2026-02-17T09:21:58Z quota_event{tenant=acme-inc} backfill=+3600000 units=minute
2026-02-17T09:22:01Z quota_apply tenant=acme-inc new_limit=600
```
anita: that backfill=+3600000 looks wrong — probably minutes vs seconds. Could be interpreted as +60 days. :grimacing:
jordan: check the migration script: I remember a change where we switched the rate denominator from minutes to hours but didn't update the backfill multiplier. @anita can you grep the migration job logs for `backfill_multiplier`?
anita: grabbing now... found in deploy logs:
```
apply_backfill(tenant, amount_minutes * 60)
```
that `* 60` is applied a second time in the migration path. bug.
maya: while we fix, customers are impacted. mitigation options: 1) revert backfill entries for acme-inc, 2) temporarily increase per-tenant limit for acme-inc in pool delta, 3) route acme-inc to another pool (canary) until fixed.
ken: option 2 is fastest: patch quota store. I can run a targeted patch: set tenant_limit=unthrottled for 10m.
jordan: be careful — unthrottled could overwhelm pool. suggest set to a high safe value (e.g., +1000 req/s) and monitor token queue depth.
maya: agreed. also enable autoscale-increase for delta:scale_factor=1.3 to give headroom.
anita: started a rollback job to remove the backfilled events for acme-inc: job id migrate-rollback-3129. targeting events with event_type=backfill and created_at >= "2026-02-17T09:20:00Z".
sre-bot: RUNBOOK: rollback job migrate-rollback-3129 started by anita at 09:45 UTC — watch pool delta CPU/GPU and 429 rate.
ken: patching tenant limit to 2000 req/s for 10m now.
maya: patch applied. 429 rate dropping from 120->18 in last 2m. :thumbsup:
jordan: good. keep rollback job running. once backfill removal completes we can remove the temporary quota bump and scale factor.
anita: rollback completed. verified removal of 3 backfill events. new quota snapshot for acme-inc shows expected baseline.
maya: confirming from prod logs: 429s back to baseline, autoscale returning to normal. letting customer know.
ken: noted for postmortem: migration script added an extra *60; add unit tests and a canary-run for quota migrations.
maya: I'll open a postmortem ticket and tag eng-migrations + eng-sre. thanks all for the quick follow-up.
